LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.6: Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: what is your father’s name? • practice pronouncing target words with correct articulation in groups. Why should we pronounce words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

2. team up to chant short singing games on family members,

3. discuss with peers the roles of various members of the nuclear family,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to identify members of the nuclear family,
2. team up to chant short singing games on family members,
3. discuss with peers the roles of various members of the nuclear family,
4. respond to simple questions to identify members of the nuclear family e.g.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner develops listening skills through actively participating in

the discussion on the roles of various members of the nuclear family.

• Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner confidently expresses themselves while chanting short singing games on family

members.

4

Values:
Integrity: This is promoted as the learner displays honesty while answering simple questions related to the nuclear family.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: This is addressed as learners demonstrate harmonious coexistence and appreciation of their peers when taking

up group tasks.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate their learning on the concept of family members to their learning in Social Studies.
